rationale: Preserves Paul's stated contrast and direct question without harmonizing it to every regime.

rationale: Preserves the time, waking, and nearer-salvation imagery.

rationale: Preserves the three paired behaviors and public daytime contrast.

rationale: Preserves household status, standing/falling wordplay, and divine ability.

rationale: Keeps the parallel denial of autonomous living and dying.

rationale: Follows the pinned verbs died and lived and preserves lordship over both groups.

rationale: Keeps both reciprocal questions and the pinned reading God's tribunal.

after: But why do you judge your brother or sister? Or why do you despise your brother or sister? For we will all stand before God's judgment seat.

rationale: Preserves oath, universal bodily homage, and verbal acknowledgment.

after: For it is written: “As I live, says the Lord, every knee will bow to me, and every tongue will confess praise to God.”

rationale: Keeps individual accountability and God as recipient.

rationale: Preserves the judge wordplay and both hindrance terms.

rationale: Keeps Paul's conviction and conscience-relative consequence.
